skill.name: webhook-tester
skill.description: Test webhook integrations locally with tunneling, inspection, signature verification, replay, and retry examples.
skill.summary: Guides local webhook testing with tunnels, receivers, signatures, replay, and retry checks.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static command-execution alerts are Markdown fence or JavaScript template-literal false positives, and the environment-variable alerts show normal secret handling examples. The skill still has meaningful operational risk because it guides public tunnel exposure and demonstrates unredacted logging or storage of webhook data.

remediation.issue: Webhook examples log complete headers and bodies.
remediation.suggestion: Add redaction for signatures, tokens, authorization headers, customer data, and payment fields before printing or storing requests.

remediation.issue: Tunnel commands expose local services to public endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before starting tunnels, prefer disposable test services, restrict access when possible, and document shutdown steps.

remediation.issue: Replay storage reads files by a supplied filename.
remediation.suggestion: Validate filenames with basename or path normalization, enforce the storage directory boundary, and reject traversal sequences.

remediation.issue: Captured webhook payloads may remain on disk after testing.
remediation.suggestion: Document retention limits, file permissions, and cleanup commands for any saved webhook request history.

semantic_findings.title: Unredacted Webhook Request Logging
semantic_findings.description: The guide logs complete request headers and bodies in multiple examples and also recommends logging all webhooks. Webhook requests can contain signatures, tokens, personal data, and payment details.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples explicitly print headers and bodies, and the best practices section says to log all webhooks. The risk is high because webhook payloads commonly include secrets or customer data.

semantic_findings.title: Public Tunnel Exposure Requires Consent
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to expose localhost through ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel, localtunnel, and VS Code forwarding. This is expected for webhook testing, but it can make local development services reachable from the internet.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines are direct tunnel setup instructions. The behavior is intentional, but exposing localhost changes the attack surface and requires explicit approval and cleanup.

semantic_findings.title: Replay Storage Example Lacks Filename Validation
semantic_findings.description: The replay example stores webhook records and later reads a file selected by filename without showing basename, normalization, or directory boundary checks. If copied into a tool with user-controlled filenames, it could read unintended files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly joins the storage directory and filename before reading the file. The impact depends on how callers supply filenames, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Webhook integrations are hard to debug when providers must reach a local service. This skill guides tunnel setup, request inspection, signature checks, replay, and retry testing.
actual_capabilities: Guides setup for ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel, localtunnel, and VS Code port forwarding.
Provides Express and Flask webhook receiver examples with signature verification.
Shows request inspection, local logging, replay, and retry simulation workflows.
Covers GitHub, Stripe, Shopify, Twilio, and Slack webhook signature details.
Includes Jest-style testing patterns for valid, invalid, and missing signatures.
limitations: It is a Markdown guide, not a packaged runnable webhook testing application.
Tunnel setup depends on external tools, accounts, and local network permissions.
Examples must be adapted before use with production webhook payloads.
Full request logging can expose sensitive data unless users add redaction.

use_cases.title: Validate a Local Webhook Endpoint
use_cases.description: Expose a local development server and confirm provider delivery, headers, payload shape, and response behavior.

use_cases.title: Test Retry and Failure Handling
use_cases.description: Simulate failed deliveries, retry attempts, and delayed success paths before a webhook integration goes live.

use_cases.title: Review Webhook Security Controls
use_cases.description: Check signature validation, replay resistance, secret handling, HTTPS use, and provider-specific verification requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Basic Local Testing
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a first webhook test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a local webhook receiver for port 3000 and explain how to inspect incoming requests safely.

prompt_templates.title: Expose a Local Endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate tunnel setup with safety checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through exposing my local webhook endpoint with a tunnel, including what permissions and cleanup steps I should use.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Signature Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me debug failing webhook signature verification for Stripe or GitHub using raw body handling and test secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Design Replay and Retry Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a webhook replay and retry test plan that covers idempotency, redaction, storage cleanup, and failure simulation.

output_examples.input: I need to test GitHub webhooks against my local development server.
output: A local receiver setup plan for the selected port.
Tunnel options with consent and cleanup notes.
A checklist for headers, signature validation, and quick responses.

output_examples.input: My Stripe webhook signature check fails during local testing.
output: A diagnosis path for raw body parsing, webhook secret selection, and signature header handling.
Provider-specific checks for test mode and endpoint configuration.
Safe logging guidance that avoids exposing payment details.

output_examples.input: I want to replay captured webhook events without leaking secrets.
output_examples.output: A replay workflow that stores only redacted test payloads, restricts replay to local endpoints, and removes logs after testing.

best_practices: Use disposable test secrets and stop public tunnels immediately after testing.
Redact signatures, tokens, customer data, and payment fields before logging or storing requests.
Verify signatures, idempotency, retry behavior, and replay protection before using real provider payloads.
anti_patterns: Do not expose a production service through a public tunnel for routine debugging.
Do not paste real customer, payment, or authentication payloads into public webhook tools.
Do not keep webhook logs that contain secrets longer than the active test requires.

faq.question: Does this skill run a tunnel automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance and examples. Users should explicitly approve any tunnel command before running it.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is webhook.site safe for sensitive payloads?
faq.answer: Use it only with test data. Public webhook tools can receive headers and payloads that may contain sensitive information.

faq.question: Does it cover signature verification?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for GitHub, Stripe, Shopify, and common provider signature headers.

faq.question: Can I copy the examples into production?
faq.answer: Treat them as development examples. Add redaction, validation, retention limits, access controls, and operational monitoring first.

faq.question: What problems does it help debug?
faq.answer: It helps inspect delivery, headers, payload formats, invalid signatures, retries, replay behavior, and provider response handling.
